text:
leah: Heads-up — ACME POC is blocked. Their SCIM sync is failing with 403 when we try to provision users into their Dedicated tenant. They want to finish before EOW.

tom: Can you paste the SCIM error payload? 403 usually means missing role/scopes on the service account or token expired.

leah: From their logs: `HTTP 403 Forbidden {\"detail\":\"service account lacks scim:write scope\"}`. They used the token we generated via the sales portal.

maya: Quick checklist: 1) Did we create a SCIM-enabled service account for Dedicated vs Hosted? 2) Confirm token was scoped for `scim:write` and `scim:read`. 3) For Private/VPC, ensure SCIM endpoint is routable from customer's IdP.

leah: We created the token from the customer "POC - AcmeCorp" entry in the console (team:dedicated). I _thought_ the portal auto-adds scim scopes.

tom: It normally does, but if the Dedicated snapshot was created before the new role mapping feature it might not. @maya can you check the service account config in the tenant?

maya: Checked — the account exists but scope only has `users:manage` (legacy). Looks like we missed the new `scim:write` scope flag. I can patch it but need a PR to update token binding for existing tokens.

onboarding-bot: Provisioning ticket created — POC-2293. Assigned to maya and tom. ETA 4h.

leah: Customer also reported SAML login flakiness — sometimes they get `NameID format mismatch` during SSO handshake. Might be separate but happening in same window.

sam: For NameID mismatch, we usually need them to set NameID format to `urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress` and map `email` claim as NameID. Ask the IdP admin to export the SAML response so we can confirm.

tom: Suggest two parallel actions: maya fixes service account scopes for SCIM token; sam helps confirm SAML NameID mapping. Leah — can you ask ACME for a SAML trace (SAMLResponse base64) and the SCIM provisioning attempt timestamps?

leah: On it. I asked for the SAML trace and the Okta System Log entries. Also requested the exact token value so we can validate scopes (they said they'd paste it in the secure chat).

maya: I'll prepare a rollback-safe update: create a new token with `scim:read,scim:write,users:manage` and rotate it into the POC tenant. If they can't paste token into chat, we can ask them to call our support UI to rotate.

sam: Security note — rotating tokens requires audit entry + customer consent. I'll pre-approve for the POC; make sure audit logging is enabled for that tenant.

tom: If SCIM still throws 403 after scope fix, check the customer's SCIM base URL. For Dedicated we expect `https://scim.<redwood-tenant-host>/v2/Users` — if they used hosted endpoint by mistake, auth will fail.

leah: ACME replied with the Okta logs and the SCIM timestamp. Their Okta shows `400` on the SAML Assertion consumer URL earlier in the day then later `200` but the NameID field is `urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:persistent`.

sam: That explains the intermittent behavior. We need them to switch to `emailAddress` or we support mapping persistent => email but that's a manual transform on our side and needs product signoff. Not ideal for a POC.

leah: Customer prefers minimal changes on their side. Can we do a quick transform for the POC while we work on a long-term fix?

maya: We can add a temporary shim in the POC gateway that checks NameID format `persistent` and attempts to lookup corresponding email via the SCIM lookup endpoint. It will be best-effort but should unblock them. Needs eng-runtime approval for the shim.

tom: I'll ping eng-runtime in #eng-runtime and include the sample SAMLResponse + logs. Tagging @runtime-lead.

onboarding-bot: Note: POC-2293 updated — scope patch planned, shim option requested, security approval pending.

leah: Customer asked about a Hosted API key so they can run quick smoke tests while we sort Dedicated. Are we okay issuing a short-lived hosted key for test traffic?

sam: We can issue a hosted, short-lived key (12h) scoped to read-only and limited token quotas. Documented and audited. OK from security for POC if we log and expire.

leah: Great — I created hosted test key and sent via secure channel. Asked them to use hosted for smoke tests and we will rotate Dedicated token once fix is deployed.

maya: Status: I created new token with `scim:read,scim:write,users:manage` and staged it for rotation. Waiting on ACME to trigger rotation or approve us to swap.

leah: ACME approved rotation. Can we schedule a 15m window to swap and watch provisioning?

tom: I can monitor. Let's do 14:00 PT. I'll be on call and watching SCIM logs.

sam: I'll monitor audit logs and confirm token scoping post-rotation.

maya: After rotation, if SCIM still 403, run this curl from their network to confirm endpoint and token scopes:

maya: ```bash
curl -s -D - -X GET \"https://scim.acme-poc.redwood.internal/v2/Users?filter=userName%20eq%20\"jane.doe\"\" \\\n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>\"
```

leah: All set for 14:00 PT. I told ACME we'll give them a 30m rollback window. Thanks everyone — will update thread after swap.

onboarding-bot: POC-2293 scheduled swap at 14:00 PT.

leah: Post-swap update: rotation succeeded, initial SCIM sync now returning 200 and users provisioned. Customer still has SAML NameID mismatch for a few legacy users; we recommended they change NameID format. For the POC it's acceptable.

tom: Awesome. Closing blocker but logging follow-ups: PROD-safe NameID mapping path, auto-scope migration for legacy tokens.

sam: I'll open security ticket for the temporary hosted key, add audit notes.

maya: I'll follow up with a small migration job to auto-add `scim:write` to tokens created before the new role flag.

leah: Thanks team — ACME now green for the demo next week. :tada:"
